info.name: Road Master API (RBAC + Exams)
info.description:
Full exercise of every implemented endpoint: auth, dynamic CASL/Spatie-style RBAC (roles/permissions/user-role assignment/effective-permissions), question-bank content management (categories/questions), exam configuration, wallet top-ups, and the complete exam-attempt lifecycle (free attempt, paid attempt, insufficient-balance rejection, scoring, pass/fail, and the one-attempt-at-a-time guard) — plus a dedicated Edge Cases folder for the negative paths (403/401/404/409/400) that a happy-path-only run never touches.

**Before running:** import `RoadMaster.postman_environment.json` and select it in the environment dropdown (top right). Every token/id captured during the run is written there — nothing needs to be copy-pasted between requests.

Run order for a full top-to-bottom Collection Runner pass:
1. **Auth** — registers the first user (becomes SuperAdmin) and a second user (becomes the seeded `client` role via DefaultRole). The first request also stamps a fresh `{{runId}}` so re-running the whole collection never collides on unique fields (emails/phones/category name).
2. **Categories** / **Questions** / **Exam Config** — SuperAdmin builds a 2-question category and an exam config priced at 500, pass mark 60%.
3. **Transactions** — client tops up their wallet.
4. **Exam Attempts** — client sits the exam 5 times back-to-back, exercising: the free first attempt, a paid attempt with a wrong answer (fails the pass mark), a paid attempt with the exact remaining balance, a paid attempt that correctly gets rejected for insufficient balance, and a final attempt left deliberately `IN_PROGRESS` so the Edge Cases folder has something to submit answers against.
5. **Permissions** / **Roles** / **Users** — the original dynamic-RBAC demo: create a permission + role, attach it, grant it to the client user, read back their effective permissions, then detach everything.
6. **App** — public health check.
7. **Advanced (use with care)** — repoints the singleton `DefaultRole`; kept out of the main run so a normal pass never changes what new registrants land in.
8. **Edge Cases & Validation** — every negative path found while wiring this up: wrong password, duplicate email, no-token 401, RBAC 403s, invalid option submission, double-complete, deleting content that's still referenced (409, by design — see the service's `mapPrismaError`), and the in-progress guard.
9. **Cleanup** — detaches/unassigns/deletes the Permissions/Roles demo data. Category/Question/ExamConfig created in this run are *not* deleted here — once an ExamAttempt references them they're FK-protected (that's exactly what the 409 tests in Edge Cases confirm), so leftover exam content across runs is expected.

exec: // Fresh run id so email/phone/category-name collisions never happen across reruns.

request.description: Only produces a SuperAdmin if the database is completely empty of users. If you've already registered a user against this database, this becomes an ordinary client-role registration instead — wipe the users/roles tables (or point at a fresh DB) if you need a real SuperAdmin bootstrap.

item.name: Register - Second User (becomes default client role)

request.description: Requires prisma/seed.ts to have been run first so a DefaultRole row exists — otherwise registration throws a 500 ('No default role is configured').

LoginDto authenticates by `phone`, not email (AuthService#login calls usersService.findByPhone). Re-login helper for after {{superAdminToken}} expires — refreshes it and {{superAdminUserId}}.

Note: this endpoint's DTO had `@IsEmail()` on the `phone` field, which rejected every real phone number and made login unusable — fixed to `@IsString()` alongside this collection update (src/auth/dto/login.dto.ts).
Refreshes {{clientToken}}/{{clientUserId}} after expiry, without re-registering (which would create a brand new user).
Category.name is @unique in the schema — suffixed with {{runId}} so re-running this collection against the same database never 409s here.
The response doesn't include the created options (question.create has no `include`) — the next request (List Questions) captures their ids instead.

exec: pm.test('question 1 found with options', () => pm.expect(q1 && q1.options.length).to.be.above(0));
pm.test('question 2 found with options', () => pm.expect(q2 && q2.options.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Admin listing — options come back with their real `isCorrect` flag (only the exam-attempt endpoints redact it while an attempt is IN_PROGRESS). This is how the collection learns which option id is the correct answer for each question, for the Exam Attempts folder below.
numberOfQuestions is pinned to 2 to match the 2 questions seeded above — Exam Attempts will pass this examConfigId + categoryId together, which draws exactly from this category.
There is no GET /exam-config/:id — only this list endpoint (same for Category and Question, which also have no get-by-id route).
Funds the client's wallet with 1000 — enough to cover two 500-priced exam fees below (attempt #1 is free regardless, so this really funds attempts #2 and #3).
Row-level scoped via accessibleBy — should show only the TOPUP above.

hasUsedFreeExam is false for a brand-new user, so this is claimed as the free attempt (compare-and-swap in ExamAttemptsService#startAttempt) regardless of the config's price — no wallet debit, no Transaction row.
While IN_PROGRESS, shapeAttempt() strips isCorrect/explanation from both answers and options. Once COMPLETED, they're revealed for review — assert that here.
hasUsedFreeExam is now true, so this debits 500 from the wallet (TransactionsService#chargeExamFee) — wallet goes from 1000 to 500.
On purpose, to prove scoring/pass-mark math below (1/2 = 50%, under the 60% pass mark).

exec: pm.test('did not pass (below 60% pass mark)', () => pm.expect(body.passed).to.eql(false));

request.description: Wallet is exactly 500 and the fee is 500 — chargeExamFee's `walletBalance: { gte: amount }` guard should allow this (>=, not >). Wallet goes to 0 after this.
Completing with zero submitted answers is allowed — every question is simply counted wrong. Confirms the exam can always be finalized even if abandoned mid-way.

Wallet is 0 after attempt #3's charge — this proves TransactionsService#chargeExamFee's compare-and-swap correctly refuses to let the balance go negative, and that no ExamAttempt row is created when the charge fails (the whole thing is one transaction).

Deliberately never completed. Feeds two things: the 'already in progress' 400 test right below, and the submit-answer validation tests in Edge Cases & Validation (which need a live IN_PROGRESS attempt to submit against).

exec: pm.test('message mentions in-progress exam', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.match(/already have an exam in progress/));

request.description: Proves the one-attempt-at-a-time guard — this check runs before payment, so it fires regardless of wallet balance. Leaves attempt #5 as the client's one lingering IN_PROGRESS attempt at the end of this run; that's expected.
Should now show: TOPUP 1000, EXAM_FEE 500 (attempt #2), EXAM_FEE 500 (attempt #3), TOPUP 1000 — attempt #1 (free) and the rejected attempt #4 leave no Transaction row.
action/subject/conditions/fields are the CASL rule stored as data — see CaslAbilityFactory for how `conditions` gets interpolated against the real user at ability-build time.
Role.name is @unique — suffixed with {{runId}} for the same reason as the Category name above.

item.name: List Users (as Client — scoped to self only)

request.description: The client role's 'read User' permission is conditioned to { id: "${user.id}" } — passes the @RequirePermission('read','User') type-level guard, but accessibleBy() then scopes the query down to just their own row. Same row-level pattern as the exam-attempts endpoint, applied to a different resource.
Gives the client user the extra 'exam-marker' role — from here on their ability is the union of the seeded 'client' role's permissions and this one, with zero code changes.
Returns the caller's fully resolved CASL rule set (union of every attached role's permissions) — the same thing a frontend would call to conditionally render UI.
@Public() route — no Authorization header needed.

⚠️ Repoints the singleton DefaultRole at {{roleId}} — every user registered after this runs gets that role instead of the seeded 'client' role. Kept out of the main run order on purpose; run only when you mean it.
Reuses the SuperAdmin's email from the Auth folder — UsersService.create maps Prisma's P2002 to a 409.
JwtAuthGuard rejects before PoliciesGuard even runs — no Authorization header, no @Public() decorator on this route.
The seeded 'client' role only has read on Category, not create — PoliciesGuard's @RequirePermission('create','Category') check fails at the ability.can() type level.
Contrast with the request above — the seeded role does grant 'read' on Category, so this succeeds.
RolesController is guarded class-wide by @RequirePermission('manage','Role') — even listing roles needs it, and the client role has no Role permissions at all.

item.name: Submit Answer - Option Doesn't Belong to Question (expect 400)

request.description: Runs against attempt #5, which the Exam Attempts folder deliberately left IN_PROGRESS. Submits Question 2's correct option id against Question 1 — must be rejected.

item.name: Submit Answer - Question Not in This Attempt (expect 400)

request.description: Random UUID that was never snapshotted into this attempt's ExamAttemptQuestion set.

item.name: Submit Answer - Multiple Options When allowMultiple=false (expect 400)

request.description: Question 1 has allowMultiple=false; submitting 2 option ids should be rejected regardless of the second id being invalid too.
Attempt #1 was already completed earlier in the Exam Attempts folder — completing it again must be rejected, not silently re-scored.

item.name: Get Attempt That Belongs to Another User (expect 404)

request.description: Counter-intuitive on purpose: the SuperAdmin token is used here, but the seeded SuperAdmin role has isSuperAdmin=true so can('manage','all') — meaning this should actually succeed (200), NOT 404. Kept as a request to sanity-check that a real SuperAdmin bypass really does see other users' rows, in contrast to the client-scoped requests elsewhere in this collection. If you swap in a token for a *non*-admin, non-owner user instead, this correctly 404s (accessibleBy excludes rows the caller's conditions don't match, and the controller's NotFoundException doesn't leak whether the row exists).

item.name: Delete Category Still Referenced by Questions (expect 409)

request.description: CategoryService#mapPrismaError turns Prisma's P2003 (FK violation) into 409 Conflict — this is why Category isn't deleted in the Cleanup folder.

item.name: Delete Question Already Used in an Attempt (expect 409)

request.description: QuestionService#mapPrismaError maps the same P2003 to a 400 here (BadRequestException, not Conflict) — an inconsistency worth noting vs. Category/ExamConfig's 409 for the identical FK-violation scenario.

exec: pm.test('rejected — FK protected (400, not 409 — see description)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

item.name: Delete Exam Config Already Used in an Attempt (expect 409)

request.description: ExamConfigService#mapPrismaError also maps P2003 to 400 here, same inconsistency as Question above.
